rationale: Correct Duquesne Light Company's ownership ledger to the current three-vehicle structure disclosed by the company in August 2026 and in its 2025 Corporate Responsibility Report. DQE Holdings' equity is held through Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. (GIC, 44.4%), Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC (Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM, 30.4%), and AIA Montana LLC (owned by APG Americas Infrastructure and CalSTRS and managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, 25.2%). The company does not identify Macquarie as a current investor, and a New York City Comptroller infrastructure-market report records Macquarie Infrastructure and Real Assets' 2016 sale of its 30.4% interest to PGGM and John Hancock. Retire the Macquarie ownership period in 2016, preserve both the APG economic-owner and Argo manager relationships without treating the shared 25.2% vehicle interest as two separate economic stakes, and clarify that Manulife's record represents the shared Three Rivers vehicle. Also correct the website, Pittsburgh headquarters, current operating description, verification date, and supporting milestone evidence. Current-company and current-report exit searches found no later sale or pending ownership transaction involving the three disclosed vehicles.

beforeImage.name: Duquesne Light Company
beforeImage.description: Duquesne Light is the regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving the Pittsburgh region. Company materials state that it serves approximately 605,000 customers in Allegheny and Beaver counties across an approximately 817-square-mile service territory. The operating model is fully utility-based, with earnings supported by regulated network investment rather than merchant power generation. Public disclosures emphasize a dense urban and suburban footprint and ongoing grid modernization and clean-energy transition work within southwestern Pennsylvania. Duquesne's current shareholder group is publicly identified on its investor site, with GIC as the largest owner and Three Rivers Utility Holdings, the Manulife and PGGM vehicle, holding a 30.4% interest; Manulife's infrastructure team links the investment to Fund I. The current consortium structure reflects ownership changes following the 2007 take-private and later secondary transfers in 2011, 2016, and 2017.

afterImage.name: Duquesne Light Company
afterImage.description: Duquesne Light Company is the regulated electric transmission and distribution utility serving more than 600,000 customers across Allegheny and Beaver counties, including Pittsburgh, over an approximately 812-square-mile service territory. The company does not generate power and maintains approximately 8,400 miles of transmission and distribution lines. Its parent, DQE Holdings LLC, discloses three current ownership vehicles: GIC affiliate Epsom Investment Pte. Ltd. at 44.4%, Manulife/John Hancock and PGGM vehicle Three Rivers Utility Holdings, LLC at 30.4%, and APG/CalSTRS vehicle AIA Montana LLC, managed by Argo Infrastructure Partners, at 25.2%. Macquarie's former infrastructure ownership was realized in 2016.
